newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam calls in ASEAN envoys over China row.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam calls in ASEAN envoys over China row.

text.p: Vietnam has called Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) ambassadors in Hanoi to an urgent briefing on its row with China over sovereignty of a potentially gas-rich offshore area, diplomats said on Thursday.

"There will be urgent consultations on this matter," said the ambassador of one country in the seven-nation ASEAN grouping. "We are going to be briefed by Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on this issue."
Ambassadors said the situation in the South China Sea would be outlined to them by Deputy Foreign Minister Vu Khoan on Thursday afternoon.
On Sunday Hanoi said it lodged a formal complaint with Beijing over drilling by China's Kan Tan III rig in an area which it said was 64.5 nautical miles off the shoreline of central Vietnam.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman in Beijing responded that the drilling rig was in Chinese waters and that its activities were both normal and above reproach.
Vietnam joined ASEAN in July 1995, a move that analysts said could strengthen its hand in sovereignty disputes with China.
However, one ambassador said ASEAN was likely to see the latest row as a bilateral issue to which the association would not add its voice.
"We don't want to have a general ASEAN reaction," he said. "It's better left to the two countries."

Vietnam and China have competing claims on areas along their 1,306-km (816-mile) land border, areas in the Tonkin Gulf and the Paracel Islands chain, which lie to the east of the latest area of dispute.
They are also among six regional claimants to the Spratly Islands.

Hanoi said at the weekend that coastguards had repeatedly sent warnings after the oil rig and accompanying vessels arrived on March 7 in an area Vietnam calls Block 113. However, drilling operations have continued.
A local foreign affairs analyst said Vietnam would call for urgent bilateral discussions with China on the problem, but was also anxious to win international support for its position.
"Vietnam will call for further talks separately about this issue," he said. "But of course the international response is very important."
